readings.title: Incident report: delayed order confirmations
readings.summary: Đọc báo cáo sự cố: hiểu diễn biến, tác động và các hành động phòng ngừa.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: This report describes an incident at Northstar Market, a fictional online shop. On Tuesday morning, several customers paid for orders but did not immediately receive confirmation emails. The website continued to accept orders, and payment processing remained available. At first, the support team thought the issue involved a few incorrect email addresses. However, similar complaints arrived from different customers within ten minutes. The incident affected confirmation messages, not the orders themselves. This distinction was important because customers needed to know whether they should try buying their items again.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: At 09:12, a support agent posted three examples in the engineering channel. Each example included an order number and the approximate payment time, but no card information. Maya, the engineer on duty, checked the email queue and found that its oldest unfinished message was eighteen minutes old. The usual delay was less than one minute. She declared an incident at 09:18 and asked another engineer, Ben, to help investigate. Maya kept responsibility for coordinating the response so that Ben could focus on the technical problem without answering every new question.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The team had released a small change to the email worker at 08:55. The change added a delivery-status check before sending a message. During normal testing, that check returned quickly. In production, however, the external status service became slow. Each worker waited for a response before handling the next message, so unfinished work gradually filled the queue. The release did not include a limit on how long the worker could wait. The engineers found no evidence that the payment service or the order database was involved in the delay.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: At 09:26, Ben suggested rolling back the worker to its previous version. Maya agreed after checking that the old version could safely read the messages already in the queue. The rollback finished at 09:31. New confirmation messages then began moving through the system, but the team did not immediately close the incident. They watched both new orders and older messages because a successful deployment alone would not prove recovery. By 09:47, the oldest message was less than one minute old again, and a test order had received its confirmation.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Support sent affected customers a short explanation while engineers monitored recovery. The message said that their orders were recorded and that they should avoid placing the same order again. It also explained that confirmation emails would arrive later than usual. Support did not promise a specific delivery time for every email because some messages were still waiting. Customers who had already placed duplicate orders were asked to contact support for help. The team used order numbers to investigate these cases instead of asking customers to share payment details in the public support channel.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The incident delayed 246 confirmation emails. No orders were lost, and the team found no duplicate charges caused by the email worker. Some customers contacted support more than once, which increased the workload for the morning shift. The report does not treat the absence of lost orders as a reason to dismiss the incident. A missing confirmation can make a completed purchase feel uncertain. It can also lead customers to repeat an action that has already succeeded. For that reason, the customer impact included confusion and additional effort as well as the measurable delay.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The review identified two gaps in the team's checks. First, the release tests covered successful responses but not a slow external service. Second, the existing alert measured the number of failed emails, while these messages were waiting rather than failing. The team will add a timeout and a test that simulates a slow response. An alert will also watch the age of the oldest queued message. These changes address separate problems: the timeout limits waiting, and the alert helps an engineer notice a growing delay before many customers report it.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Maya will own the new queue-age alert, and Ben will own the timeout and its tests. Both changes are due before the next worker release. The review deliberately focuses on system conditions rather than blaming the person who approved the change. The approval followed the checks available at the time, but those checks were incomplete. At the next engineering meeting, the team will review whether other background workers make similar calls to external services. The incident is considered resolved, while the prevention tasks remain open and will be tracked separately.

readings.title: Code review: a useful comment at the right time
readings.summary: Đọc trao đổi review code và phân biệt lỗi cần sửa với đề xuất có thể làm sau.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The following account describes a code review at a fictional company called Fieldnote. Its application helps small teams manage customer requests. Linh, a developer, opened a pull request to add a search filter to the request list. Users would be able to choose a date range and see only requests created during that period. The feature had been requested by the support team because the existing list was becoming difficult to scan. Linh included screenshots and a short description of the change so reviewers could understand the user problem before reading the code.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The team expected reviewers to respond within one working day, although that did not mean every pull request would be approved immediately. Omar, the first reviewer, began with the description and then ran the application locally. He selected a start date and an end date and compared the results with several sample requests. The normal case worked, but a request created late on the final day was missing. Omar wrote down the exact dates he had selected and the time of the missing request. This gave Linh a clear example that she could reproduce.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The filter treated the end date as midnight at the beginning of that day. As a result, requests created later on the same day were excluded. Omar marked this as a blocking issue because it changed the meaning of the date range shown to users. His comment described the observed result, explained the expected result, and asked Linh to add a test for a request near the end of the day. He avoided a general comment such as “this looks wrong”, which would have required Linh to guess what he had actually noticed.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Another comment concerned a function name. Omar thought that “applyRange” was less clear than “filterByCreationDate”. He labelled the suggestion as optional because the current name did not cause incorrect results and was consistent with nearby code. Linh agreed that the longer name was easier to understand, but she decided to keep the existing naming style for this change. The team accepted that decision. Their review guide asks people to separate required fixes from preferences so that an author does not spend time treating every suggestion as a release blocker.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: A second reviewer, Mei, checked how the feature would be used with a keyboard. The date controls had visible labels, but the clear-filter button had only a small icon. A screen reader announced it as an unnamed button. Mei asked for an accessible label and explained why the icon alone was insufficient. This was also a required fix. The team considered accessibility part of the feature's normal behavior, rather than an improvement to add only if time remained. Linh added the label and described the change in a reply to Mei's comment.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Linh fixed the end-date logic and added two tests: one for a request late on the final day and another for a request just outside the selected range. She also updated the pull-request description with a brief note about the discovered issue. Instead of replying only “done”, she linked to the relevant change and explained the new behavior. Omar reran his original example and checked the tests. Mei repeated the keyboard and screen-reader check. Both reviewers then approved the pull request, which was merged after the automated checks passed.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The review took longer than Linh had expected, but most of the extra time came from reproducing and correcting specific problems. There was no long discussion about personal coding style. At the team's weekly meeting, Linh said that the clear distinction between required and optional comments helped her plan the work. Omar suggested adding an end-of-day case to the team's feature checklist. The team agreed to try this for date-related changes, while keeping the checklist short enough that developers would actually use it during everyday work.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: The example illustrates how a code review can serve both quality and learning. A useful comment gives the author enough context to act and identifies whether the issue must be resolved before merging. Reviewers do not need to rewrite the feature themselves, and authors do not need to accept every preference. However, the team still expects authors to acknowledge comments and explain decisions that affect the result. In this case, the final code changed in two important ways, and the discussion also created a reusable reminder for future date filters.

readings.title: Remote handover: leaving enough context
readings.summary: Đọc ghi chú bàn giao từ xa, xác định việc đã xong, việc đang chờ và người phụ trách.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: At the fictional company Harbour Tools, the engineering team works across two time zones. The morning in one office overlaps with the afternoon in another for only an hour. On Thursday, Ana needed to leave before the usual overlap meeting because of a personal appointment. She was preparing an export feature that allowed customers to download a monthly activity report. Rather than sending a short message saying “the export is nearly ready”, she wrote a handover note that another engineer could use without waiting for her to return.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Ana began the note with the goal and the current state. The download endpoint was complete, and the automated tests passed on her branch. The export page was also connected to the endpoint, but one browser check remained unfinished. She separated completed work from work that still needed attention because “nearly ready” could mean different things to different people. She included links to the branch, the pull request, and the test report. These links allowed the next engineer to inspect the actual work rather than relying entirely on her summary.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The remaining check involved downloading a large report in the team's supported mobile browser. Ana had tested a small report successfully, but a larger sample sometimes produced an empty file. She had not yet established whether the problem came from the application or the browser. Her note described the device, the browser version, the sample account, and the steps she had followed. She labelled her idea about the cause as a hypothesis, not a confirmed finding. This helped the next engineer avoid treating an early guess as a fact.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Ana then set out the next action. The incoming engineer should repeat the large-report test and attach the result to the pull request. If the file was still empty, the feature should stay behind its existing feature flag. The flag allowed the team to keep the new code available internally without showing the download option to all customers. Ana explicitly said not to enable the feature for customers until the check passed. She also named Ravi as the decision-maker if the team needed to change the release plan during her absence.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The note included one practical warning about the sample account. It contained realistic test data, but no real customer records. Engineers should not replace it with a customer account simply to obtain a larger report. Ana pointed to a script that could generate additional test activity. She also reminded the team that generated files should be attached only to the internal pull request. These details were relevant to the task because the next engineer needed enough data to reproduce the issue without exposing information from a customer's report.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: When Noah began his shift, he read the note and replied with a short acknowledgement. He repeated the remaining action in his own words and said that he would post the result by 14:00 in his local time. Ana did not need to respond for him to start. Noah reproduced the empty file, then compared the network response with the downloaded file. The server response contained the expected data, while the file saved by the browser was empty. He added that observation to the pull request without claiming that he had already found the final cause.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Ravi reviewed Noah's update and decided to delay customer access until the following week. The team could still demonstrate the feature internally using a browser that had passed the check. Support received a short update about the delay and the reason, so they would not announce the feature prematurely. When Ana returned the next morning, she read the discussion before starting further work. She did not have to ask several people what had happened during her absence because the decision and the new observations were recorded in the same place.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: The team later used Ana's note as a model for other handovers. Their template asked for the goal, completed work, open questions, the next action, and the person who could make a decision. It did not require a detailed diary of every step taken during the day. A handover is useful when it reduces uncertainty for the next person. In this example, clear limits mattered as much as technical detail: Noah knew what to test, what evidence to record, and which release decision he should leave to Ravi.

readings.title: Integration note: connecting a delivery API
readings.summary: Đọc tài liệu tích hợp API giao hàng: giới hạn thử nghiệm, retry và bảo vệ thao tác tạo đơn.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: This integration note belongs to a fictional retailer, Willow Home, which is connecting its order system to a delivery provider called ParcelWay. Staff currently copy delivery details into the provider's website, a process that takes time and sometimes introduces typing mistakes. The new integration will create delivery bookings directly from confirmed orders. The first release will support domestic standard delivery only. International and express services are outside the initial scope, even though the provider's API offers them. Keeping the scope narrow allows the team to verify the most common workflow first.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Development begins in the provider's sandbox environment. It accepts test bookings and returns sample tracking numbers, but it does not arrange real collections. The sandbox uses different credentials from the production environment. The team will store both sets of credentials in its secret manager rather than in source code or a shared spreadsheet. Developers may share the name of a missing configuration value when asking for help, but they should not paste the credential itself into a chat message. This makes troubleshooting possible without turning an ordinary conversation into a record of access secrets.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Before sending a booking request, the application checks the required address fields. A missing street name or postal code should produce a clear message for the staff member preparing the order. The integration should not send an incomplete address and hope that the provider will repair it. However, the team will avoid rewriting valid customer addresses automatically. Some unusual-looking address lines may be correct. The goal is to catch missing information, not to force every address into a format that happens to look familiar to the developers.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The application must also handle a response that arrives too late. Suppose a booking request reaches ParcelWay, but the connection closes before Willow Home receives the result. Sending the same request again could create a second booking unless the provider can recognise the repeated operation. Each booking attempt therefore includes an idempotency key derived from the order's delivery request. The same key is reused when that operation is retried. A new key is created only when staff intentionally create a different delivery request, not simply because the network response was missing.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Not every error should trigger a retry. If ParcelWay reports that a required field is invalid, repeating the unchanged request will not help. The application should show the problem to staff and wait for a correction. Temporary failures, such as a short period of service unavailability, can be retried with increasing delays. The first release permits at most three automatic attempts for one booking operation. After that, the order remains visible in a queue for manual attention. This limit prevents a persistent problem from generating an endless stream of requests.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The provider limits how quickly clients may send requests. During a bulk export of delivery bookings, the application must spread the requests over time instead of sending them all at once. If the provider returns a rate-limit response with a suggested waiting period, the application will respect that period before trying again. Staff will see a “waiting to book” status while work is queued. That status is different from “booking failed”, because waiting does not yet indicate a permanent problem. The page should make this difference clear without requiring staff to understand HTTP response codes.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The operations team needs enough information to investigate failures. Logs will include the internal order reference, the operation status, and the provider's request identifier when one is available. They will not include the full customer address or access credentials. A booking is considered successful only when the provider returns a booking reference, which is saved on the order. A successful HTTP connection alone is not enough. Staff can use the saved reference to find the delivery in the provider's portal, and support can use it when asking the provider about a specific booking.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Before production access is enabled, the team will run a small set of scenarios: a normal booking, an invalid address, a temporary failure, a repeated request, and a rate-limit response. Sandbox success will be followed by a limited production trial with five real orders approved by operations. During that trial, a staff member will compare each saved booking reference with the provider's portal. The integration will expand only after those records match and the team confirms that duplicate retries do not create extra bookings. The rollout decision belongs to the operations lead and the engineering lead together.

readings.title: Planning memo: choosing what fits in a sprint
readings.summary: Đọc bản ghi quyết định sprint: cân đối nhu cầu, khả năng thực hiện và tiêu chí thành công.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The product team at the fictional company ClearDesk is preparing its next sprint, which will last two weeks. Three pieces of work are competing for attention: a fix for unreliable file uploads, a dashboard requested by sales, and an improvement to the onboarding emails. Each has a supporter, and all three could help customers. However, two engineers will be away for part of the sprint, so the team cannot simply accept every request. The planning memo records the trade-offs and the final decision so that people outside engineering understand what the team expects to deliver.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The upload problem affects customers who attach large documents to a request. Some uploads stop without showing a useful error message, leaving customers unsure whether they should try again. Support recorded seventeen related conversations during the previous week. The exact number of affected customers is unknown because not everyone contacts support. The team therefore treats the conversations as evidence of a problem, rather than as a complete measurement of its size. An engineer has already reproduced the issue with a test file, making the next investigation step reasonably clear.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Sales wants a dashboard that shows weekly activity for each customer account. The request comes from discussions with two potential customers, both of whom asked how managers could monitor usage. A complete dashboard would require agreement about the metrics, new data queries, and a page design. The team has not yet confirmed whether the same metrics would be useful to existing customers. Building the whole page immediately would commit considerable effort before that question is answered. Sales agrees to help organise short interviews instead of expecting a finished dashboard this sprint.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The onboarding email improvement is smaller, but it still needs coordination. The current sequence tells new users about several features without explaining which action to take first. The proposal is to replace the first message with a clearer invitation to create one request. Marketing can draft the message, while engineering must update the sending rule and verify that existing users do not receive it again. This work is not urgent in the same way as the upload issue, but the team believes it can fit after the investigation and the essential upload fix.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: During planning, the engineers avoid giving precise estimates for work they have not understood. They divide the upload task into an investigation and a fix, with a review after the first day. If the investigation reveals a larger problem, they will reduce the email work rather than silently extending the sprint. The product manager records this fallback in the memo. A fallback is useful only if the people requesting the work know about it in advance. It allows the team to make a controlled adjustment instead of surprising stakeholders near the deadline.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The final sprint goal is to make document submission more reliable and reduce uncertainty when an upload cannot complete. Success will be checked with a file that previously reproduced the problem, a normal small file, and a deliberately interrupted connection. The team also wants the customer-facing error to explain what to do next. Finishing a technical change without checking the message would not fully meet the goal. Support will review the wording because they understand the questions customers ask when a document appears to disappear during submission.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The dashboard remains outside the delivery commitment. Instead, the product manager and a sales colleague will interview four existing customers about the information managers actually need. They will bring a short summary to the next planning meeting. This discovery work can influence a later sprint, but it is not presented as a promise to build the dashboard. The email change is included as a secondary item and can be reduced if the upload investigation takes longer than expected. The memo clearly separates the main goal from this conditional piece of work.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: At the end of planning, the team shares the memo with support, sales, and marketing. Questions are welcome, especially if someone knows about a deadline or customer commitment that has not been discussed. Once the sprint begins, new requests will still be recorded, but they will not automatically enter the active plan. The product manager and engineering lead will review any urgent request together and explain what would need to move. The plan is a realistic agreement based on current information, with a visible way to change it when that information changes.

readings.title: Before You Sign: An Apartment Viewing Guide
readings.summary: Đọc hướng dẫn thuê căn hộ, kiểm tra chi phí, giấy tờ và bàn giao trước khi ký.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: A listing for Green Court Apartments describes the building as a quiet place within walking distance of the station. That description may be useful, but it does not answer every question a future resident should ask. The following guide was prepared for people attending a viewing with the building's rental team. It explains the process from making an appointment to collecting keys. Visitors are encouraged to take notes and compare the written information with what they see. A friendly conversation during a viewing does not replace the terms in a signed agreement.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Viewings normally take place between Tuesday and Saturday. You can request a time by email, giving your name, telephone number, and preferred moving date. The team sends a confirmation that includes the apartment number and the meeting point outside reception. A viewing lasts about thirty minutes. If you arrive late, the agent may need to shorten the visit because another appointment follows. You may bring a friend, but please mention this in your reply. The reception desk cannot arrange an immediate viewing for someone who arrives without an appointment.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: During the visit, check the things that will affect your normal routine. Turn on taps, look for marks around windows, and ask permission before opening cupboards. Try standing in the bedroom with the window closed to judge the noise from the road. The agent can show where washing machines are connected, but the apartment is supplied without a washing machine. Photographs are permitted inside the empty unit. Avoid photographing other residents or their belongings in shared areas. If something needs repair, ask for its condition and the planned repair date to be recorded.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The advertised rent covers the apartment and access to the bicycle room. Electricity, water, and internet are paid separately by the resident. A monthly building service charge covers cleaning of shared spaces and maintenance of the lift. Ask for an example of the total monthly cost rather than comparing rent alone. Previous residents' electricity bills can indicate a possible range, although your own use may differ. Parking spaces are limited and require a separate agreement. Do not assume that an empty space seen during your visit is included or will remain available.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: People who wish to apply complete a short form and provide proof of identity and income. The team checks applications in the order in which complete documents arrive. Sending only the form does not reserve the apartment. Successful applicants receive a draft rental agreement by email and have two working days to review it. Read the sections about ending the tenancy, visitors, and repairs carefully. Questions can be sent to the rental team before you sign. The building does not require applicants to pay an application fee or buy a special inspection report.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The security deposit is equal to one month's rent. It is paid after the agreement has been signed, together with the first rental payment. A receipt is sent when the transfer reaches the account stated in the agreement. Never rely on account details sent from an unfamiliar address without checking them with the team. The deposit is not the final month's rent. At the end of the tenancy, the apartment's condition is compared with the move-in record, and the team explains any proposed deduction in writing before returning the remaining money.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: On moving day, the resident and agent complete an inventory together. This record lists furniture, appliances, meter readings, and existing damage. A small scratch is easier to discuss before furniture and boxes fill the room. Residents have three days after receiving the keys to report anything missed during the inspection. Send photographs and a clear description by email so that they can be attached to the record. Keep your own copy of the completed inventory. This helps both sides distinguish earlier damage from a problem that appeared during the tenancy.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: After moving in, routine repair requests should be submitted through the resident portal. Describe what happened, when you noticed it, and whether the problem prevents normal use of the room. The team replies within two working days, although the actual repair may take longer if parts are needed. Urgent building problems use the telephone number displayed near reception. Residents should also read the shared-space rules, including the hours for noisy moving work. Planning a delivery within those hours makes moving easier for the new resident and for neighbours who already live there.

readings.title: A Clinic Appointment Without the Confusion
readings.summary: Đọc thông báo về đặt lịch khám, giờ đến, phiên dịch và thủ tục thanh toán; tập trung vào quy trình.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Riverside Clinic has introduced a new appointment system after visitors reported confusion about booking messages and arrival times. This information sheet explains the practical arrangements for an ordinary appointment. It does not give advice about symptoms or treatment. Different services may send additional instructions, so patients should read every message connected with their booking. The clinic hopes that clearer information will reduce unnecessary journeys and help reception staff support visitors who need assistance. Anyone uncertain about an instruction can contact the booking team before the day of their visit.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Appointments can be requested through the clinic website or by telephone during office hours. Online users choose a service and a preferred time, then submit their contact details. The first message confirms only that the request has been received. A second message confirms the appointment itself. Do not treat the first message as a booking confirmation. If the requested time is unavailable, the team offers another option. Patients should check that the name and telephone number in the confirmation are correct, especially when someone else has made the request on their behalf.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The confirmation gives both the appointment time and the recommended arrival time. Patients should arrive fifteen minutes before their appointment. This allows time to check personal details and complete any forms requested by the service. Arriving much earlier does not move the appointment forward. Visitors who know they will be late should telephone reception rather than send a message through the booking website. The receptionist can check whether the appointment can still take place or whether another time is needed. The decision depends on the schedule for that particular service.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Bring a form of identification and any documents specifically listed in the confirmation. If your address or contact number has changed, tell reception when you check in. The clinic uses these details to send follow-up booking information, so an old number can cause problems later. A patient who has completed an online form should still bring the reference number from the confirmation. Reception can use it to find the booking quickly. Printed copies are welcome, but visitors may also show the reference number on their phone at the desk.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Patients who need an interpreter should request one when arranging the appointment. The booking team needs at least three working days to arrange an interpreter. Include the language required and whether you prefer telephone or in-person support. The team confirms which option is available before the appointment. Visitors should not assume that someone at reception speaks their language. A family member may accompany a patient, but the clinic asks patients to discuss interpretation needs with the booking team so that important information can be communicated clearly throughout the visit.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The main entrance is on Bridge Road, next to the small public library. The entrance facing the car park is used by staff and deliveries. A ramp beside the main entrance provides access for visitors who use wheelchairs or have difficulty with steps. A bus stop is located across the road. The clinic has no visitor parking spaces, so drivers should allow time to find public parking nearby. Visitors needing help at the entrance can call the reception number in their confirmation. Staff can explain the route from the street to the waiting area.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Payment arrangements vary by service and are stated in the appointment confirmation. Where a payment is required, patients receive an itemised receipt. Questions about fees should be raised with the booking team before the visit, particularly if a patient is unsure which service has been booked. Reception accepts bank cards but does not accept cash. A companion may pay on the patient's behalf. However, making a payment does not give that person access to private appointment information. The team will follow the clinic's consent process when someone requests information for another adult.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: If your plans change, use the cancellation link in the confirmation or telephone the booking team. Please cancel at least twenty-four hours before the appointment where possible. This gives the team time to offer the slot to someone else. Cancelling does not automatically create a new booking; you must request another appointment separately. After your visit, check any new booking message carefully. A recommendation to return on a certain date and a confirmed appointment are different things. Keeping the messages together makes it easier to know what has actually been arranged.

readings.title: Your Bus Route Is Changing on Monday
readings.summary: Đọc thông báo đổi tuyến xe buýt để xác định trạm tạm, vé, giờ cao điểm và cách cập nhật.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: From Monday 6 April, the fictional Eastbank Transport service will change the route of bus 42 while the council replaces pipes under Market Street. The work is expected to last six weeks. This notice explains the temporary route, the stops that will close, and the options for passengers travelling to the shopping district. Other Eastbank bus routes will continue as usual unless a separate notice is published. Passengers should check their journey before travelling because familiar landmarks may no longer indicate the correct place to wait for bus 42.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Between Central Station and River Park, bus 42 will use King Road instead of Market Street. The rest of the route is unchanged. The stops outside Market Hall and West Pharmacy will not be served during the work. A temporary stop will operate beside the King Road post office in both directions. Yellow signs will show where passengers should queue. Please use the signed stop even if you can see the bus passing somewhere closer. Drivers can only pick up and drop off passengers at authorised stops along the temporary route.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Passengers going to Market Hall can leave the bus at the post office and follow the signed walking route through Pine Lane. The walk takes about eight minutes at an ordinary pace. The council has placed temporary lighting along the lane, but passengers should still take care at the crossing near the loading entrance. Those who prefer a shorter walk can remain on the bus until Library Square and change to route 7. That service stops near the east entrance of Market Hall, although changing buses may increase the total journey time.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The first and last departures from each end of the route remain the same. However, the temporary route adds approximately ten minutes to a full journey between Central Station and River Park. During the morning peak, buses will run every twelve minutes instead of every ten minutes. Outside the morning peak, the published frequency is unchanged. A timetable marked 'temporary April service' is available on the website and at the station information desk. Passengers with a connection to a train should allow additional time rather than relying on their previous routine.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Existing tickets and travel cards remain valid on bus 42. Passengers changing to route 7 at Library Square may use the same ticket if the second journey begins within sixty minutes of the first boarding. Show the original ticket to the second driver or tap the same travel card. A ticket bought for only one route must still meet the normal rules for the first journey. Anyone unsure about a particular ticket can ask at the information desk before boarding. Drivers cannot correct an earlier ticket purchase while the bus is moving.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Most buses on the route have space for one wheelchair, subject to availability. The temporary post office stop has a raised kerb and a clear boarding area. However, the walking route through Pine Lane includes a narrow section that some passengers may find inconvenient. Passengers requiring step-free access to Market Hall are advised to use the connection at Library Square. The information desk can explain this journey and provide a printed route map. This advice concerns access along the route; it does not guarantee that a wheelchair space will be free on every departure.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The journey planner will display the temporary route from the Sunday evening before the change. If you saved a journey earlier in the week, search again to make sure it includes the diversion. Electronic displays at closed stops may be switched off during the work. A paper notice at each closed stop will direct passengers to the nearest alternative. Eastbank will publish weekly updates on the transport website. If the construction schedule changes, the end date of the diversion will be updated there before signs are removed from the temporary stops.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Transport staff will be present at Central Station and the post office stop during the first two weekday morning peaks. They can help passengers find the queue and understand the new timetable. After that period, questions can be sent through the website or raised at the station desk. When reporting a problem, include the date, approximate time, direction of travel, and stop name. This detail helps the team investigate whether the issue relates to the diversion, traffic, or a particular departure. A general comment that a bus was late is harder to check.

readings.title: Your First Week on a Software Team
readings.summary: Đọc kế hoạch hội nhập của kỹ sư mới: tài khoản, môi trường thử nghiệm, họp nhóm và thay đổi đầu tiên.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Welcome to the Harbour software team. This first-week guide is intended to help new engineers understand how work moves through the team before they take responsibility for a large task. The aim is steady progress, not completing the longest possible list of activities. Your manager will adapt the schedule if equipment or access takes longer than expected. Keep a short note of questions as they arise. A question that seems small to a new colleague may reveal an unclear instruction that has confused several people before.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: On Monday morning, collect your laptop from the support desk and check the equipment list before signing the receipt. The support team will help you set up your company account and multi-factor authentication. Use the password manager provided by the company for work credentials. Do not ask a colleague to share their login while you wait for access. If an account request is delayed, tell your manager and record the request number. You can spend the waiting time reading the project overview or discussing the product with your onboarding partner.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Each new engineer is paired with an onboarding partner for the first month. This person helps explain team routines and shows where useful information is stored. They are not responsible for approving every decision you make. Your manager remains the contact for priorities and workload. Arrange a short meeting with your partner on each of the first three days, then agree on a schedule that works for both of you. When asking for help, explain what you tried and what happened. This makes it easier to identify the missing step.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Before making a code change, set up the local development environment using the repository guide. Run the sample application and confirm that its basic checks pass. The training database contains fictional customer records. New starters should use that database for their initial experiments. Access to the live production system requires separate approval and is not part of the standard first-day setup. If an instruction appears to require real customer data, stop and ask your partner to check it. Screenshots shared in team discussions should also avoid exposing account details or private information.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The team holds a fifteen-minute planning meeting at nine thirty each morning. Each person briefly explains current work, a likely next step, and anything blocking progress. You do not need to give a long report or pretend that a blocked task is going well. If an issue needs detailed discussion, arrange a separate conversation after the meeting. Written notes are available for colleagues who cannot attend. New starters may listen during their first meeting, but should prepare a short update once they have begun their first task.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Your first code task should be small enough to understand and review within a few days. Common examples include correcting a confusing error message or adding a check for an already documented behaviour. Discuss the expected outcome with your manager before starting. Create a branch and open a draft change request early so that others can see your approach. Include the reason for the change, the behaviour before and after it, and the checks you ran. A short explanation grounded in a concrete example is more useful than a long list of files.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: A reviewer may request changes or ask why you chose a particular approach. Treat these questions as part of improving the shared code, rather than as a test of whether you belong on the team. If a comment is unclear, ask for an example. After updating the code, reply to the relevant discussion so the reviewer knows what changed. Approval alone does not mean that a change has been released to users. The team follows a separate release process, and your partner will explain how to find the status of a merged change.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: At the end of Friday, meet your manager for a short check-in. Discuss what you can now do independently, what still needs support, and whether the schedule was realistic. This is also the time to report missing access that has not been resolved. Keep your questions and useful links in a personal onboarding note, but move corrections to shared instructions into the team documentation. Future starters benefit when the guide improves. There is no requirement to deliver a production feature in the first week; understanding the workflow is a valuable result in itself.

readings.title: Choosing a Laptop Repair Service
readings.summary: Đọc hướng dẫn so sánh dịch vụ sửa laptop: phí kiểm tra, báo giá, dữ liệu, bảo hành và nhận máy.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: When a laptop stops working reliably, choosing a repair service can feel urgent, especially if the device is used for work or study. However, the fastest promise is not always the clearest offer. This fictional consumer guide explains what to compare before handing over a device. It focuses on the repair process rather than on instructions for fixing hardware yourself. A useful service should explain what it will inspect, what you may need to pay, and how it will ask for approval. Those details make different offers easier to compare.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Begin by describing the problem as precisely as you can. Write down when it started, what you were doing, and whether it happens every time or only occasionally. For example, 'the screen goes dark after about twenty minutes' gives more information than 'the laptop is broken'. Mention any recent changes, such as a new charger or an operating system update, without assuming that the change caused the fault. A technician may still need to inspect the device. Your description helps the service decide which checks are relevant and explain the next steps.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Ask whether the service charges an inspection fee before repairs are approved. Some shops charge for diagnosis even when the customer decides not to continue. Others include that cost in the repair price only if the repair goes ahead. An advertised free check may cover a brief external inspection rather than a full investigation. Request the conditions in writing so that you understand the difference. If the service gives a price before seeing the laptop, ask whether it is an estimate or a fixed quote and what could make the amount change.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: A written quote should identify the proposed work, parts, labour, and any delivery charge. It should also state whether replacement parts are new or previously used. Compare the total amount and the scope of the work, rather than choosing only the lowest headline price. Ask the service to contact you before carrying out extra work. A technician may discover a second problem during inspection, but that does not automatically give permission to repair it. Agree on the maximum amount you authorise and on the best telephone number or email address for further approval.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Before handing over the laptop, ask what access the technician needs and how customer data is handled. If the device still allows it, make a backup of important files and check that the backup opens on another device. A repair service cannot promise that every repair will preserve all stored data. Avoid giving account passwords casually over an open counter. If access is necessary, ask whether a temporary account can be used. Remove accessories that are not needed for the inspection, and list any charger or other item that remains with the laptop.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Completion times depend on the fault, the availability of parts, and the current queue. Ask whether a promised date means diagnosis will be complete or the repaired device will be ready for collection. Those are different stages. A shop may identify the problem quickly but then wait several days for a part. If you have an important deadline, explain it before agreeing to the repair. Ask how you will receive updates if the schedule changes. A clear update policy is more useful than a vague assurance that the job should be finished soon.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Before accepting the quote, read the repair warranty. It should explain which work or parts are covered, how long the cover lasts, and how to report a problem. A warranty on a replaced keyboard does not necessarily cover an unrelated battery fault. Ask whether returning the device for a covered issue involves another inspection charge. Keep the quote, receipt, and any messages describing the work. If the same problem returns, these records help you explain what was previously reported and what the technician said had been repaired.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: When collecting the laptop, allow time to review the completed work. Ask the technician to show that the original fault has been checked, and test the relevant function if possible. Compare the invoice with the quote and ask about any difference before leaving. Check that the charger and other listed accessories are returned. If you cannot test something at the counter, ask how soon you should report a problem found at home. Keep a brief record of the collection date and the test you performed. This provides a clear starting point if further discussion becomes necessary.

readings.title: Migration proposal: giving the test database a clean start
readings.summary: Nhóm kỹ thuật đề xuất thay cơ sở dữ liệu kiểm thử dùng chung bằng môi trường riêng cho từng nhóm. Bài đọc giải thích vấn đề hiện tại, chi phí, giới hạn của thử nghiệm và điều kiện để tiếp tục triển khai.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: For the past year, three engineering teams at Cedar Market have used one shared database for testing. This arrangement was easy to set up when the company had only six developers. Now there are eighteen, and their work often overlaps. On Tuesday, a developer testing a discount rule changed several customer records. An hour later, another team reported that its account tests were failing. Nothing was wrong with the account code; the expected records had changed. The incident did not affect real customers, but four people spent the afternoon investigating it. This proposal explains how separate test databases could reduce that kind of interruption.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The proposed arrangement gives each team its own database, created from the same approved starting dataset. A small script would prepare the database and add fictional accounts, products, and orders. Developers could then change these records without surprising another team. The proposal does not include a separate database for every developer because the current equipment cannot support that many active copies comfortably. Team members would still need to coordinate with one another. However, the people sharing a database would be working on related tasks, so discussing changes should be easier. The script would also record which version of the starting dataset it used.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The starting dataset needs careful attention. The current database contains years of old test records, including products that no longer exist and accounts with unclear purposes. Copying all of it would preserve the confusion. Instead, Linh and Omar will build a smaller set that covers common purchases, cancelled orders, and accounts with different permission levels. They will use fictional information throughout. A support specialist will review the examples because unusual customer situations are sometimes missing from engineering tests. The first version will not represent every possible case, but teams can request additions when they explain which behaviour they need to test.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: There are costs as well as benefits. Preparing the script and reviewing the data will take about three working days, during which two planned interface improvements will move to the next sprint. Storage use will rise, although the team does not yet have a reliable estimate. To measure it, the billing team will try the new arrangement for one week. Its database will be recreated each morning, and the team will record the space used after a normal day of work. This pilot should also reveal whether the preparation process is slow enough to interrupt daily development. These measurements will guide the final decision.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Some tests require information to remain available for several days. For example, the billing team checks what happens when an unpaid order receives a reminder later in the week. A daily reset would remove that order before the test finished. During the pilot, a clearly named folder will hold the instructions for these longer tests. The preparation script can rebuild their required records after a reset. This approach requires extra work, but it makes the test conditions visible to everyone. It also avoids a growing collection of records that nobody remembers creating. Tests that cannot be rebuilt this way must be listed before the pilot begins.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The change will be introduced gradually. On Friday afternoon, Linh will demonstrate the preparation script and ask each team to run it once. The shared database will remain available during the pilot. Teams must label bug reports with the database they used so that reviewers can understand the circumstances. If the new script fails, the billing team can return to the shared database while Linh investigates. No production settings will change as part of this work. After the pilot, the three team leads will compare interruptions, preparation time, and storage use. They will also collect comments from developers who joined the company recently.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The recommendation is to continue only if the pilot produces clear practical improvements. A perfect starting dataset is not the goal; a predictable one is. If separate databases reduce interruptions but take too long to prepare, the team should improve the script before expanding the system. If the benefits are small, keeping the shared arrangement may be reasonable for now. Whatever the decision, the reviewed dataset and written test instructions will remain useful. The team leads will publish their decision the following Wednesday, including the measurements and any unresolved concerns. This will help colleagues understand both the outcome and the reasons behind it.

readings.title: Workplace procedure: making shared desks easier to use
readings.summary: Văn phòng thử nghiệm quy trình đặt bàn dùng chung. Bài đọc trình bày cách đặt chỗ, xử lý thay đổi, bảo quản đồ đạc và đánh giá hiệu quả mà vẫn đáp ứng nhu cầu làm việc khác nhau.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: When Northbank Studio moved into its smaller office, managers expected the shared desks to be simple to use. Most employees worked at home two days a week, so there seemed to be enough space. During the first month, however, people often arrived to find bags on empty desks and no clear information about who was coming in. Others booked a meeting room just to have somewhere to sit. The office team has now prepared a four-week trial procedure. Its purpose is to make available space easier to find while allowing people to change their plans when work or travel arrangements change unexpectedly.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Employees should book a desk through the office calendar by four in the afternoon on the previous working day. Each desk has a number and a short description of its equipment. Someone who needs an extra monitor can therefore choose a suitable place before travelling. Bookings cover either a morning, an afternoon, or a full day. A full-day booking does not include a meeting room. People attending the same project meeting may choose nearby desks, but they should avoid reserving additional places for colleagues who have not confirmed their attendance. The calendar is intended to show actual plans rather than possible demand.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: On arrival, employees should mark their booking as active using the tablet near reception. A morning booking becomes available to others at ten if its owner has not checked in or contacted the office team. This gives someone delayed by transport a way to keep the desk without leaving it empty indefinitely. Afternoon bookings follow the same rule after two. Employees who decide to work from home should cancel as soon as they know. If the calendar is unavailable, reception will keep a paper list and enter the changes later. Nobody needs to create a second booking while that temporary list is being used.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The desks are divided into two areas with different expectations. The window area is for quiet work, while the area near the kitchen allows short conversations. Calls lasting more than five minutes should move to a phone room when one is available. These arrangements will not remove every distraction, but they give employees useful information when choosing a desk. People should use headphones for audio and keep shared walkways clear. Anyone who needs a particular working arrangement should contact the office coordinator privately. The coordinator will discuss a suitable option without adding personal details to the public booking calendar or asking colleagues to explain their needs.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Personal items should go into lockers when an employee leaves for the day. Each locker can be used for up to one working week, after which it should be emptied or renewed through reception. This prevents a small number of people from holding all the storage space. Desk drawers are for shared supplies, including spare cables and notebooks. At the end of a booking, employees should remove their papers, wipe the surface, and return the chair to its original position. A forgotten item will be placed in the collection box behind reception. The office team will record where it was found to make collection easier.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Visitors and unexpected attendance need a separate plan. Two desks near reception will remain outside the normal booking system for visiting colleagues or employees called in at short notice. These desks can be assigned by reception on the day, but they cannot be reserved in advance by a project team. If every suitable desk is occupied, the office coordinator will discuss another work location with the employee concerned. Meeting rooms should remain available for meetings. Managers must also avoid asking an entire team to attend without first checking space. A calendar full of individual bookings cannot easily absorb a last-minute group arrival.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The office team will review the trial every Friday using cancelled bookings, unused reservations, and reports of unavailable equipment. Employees can leave a short comment in the calendar, but urgent problems should go directly to reception. The review will consider convenience as well as the number of occupied desks. A system that fills every place but makes focused work difficult would not be a success. After four weeks, employees will receive a short survey and an explanation of any changes. Until then, the procedure is a shared experiment: people should follow it consistently and report problems early enough for the office team to respond.

readings.title: Building notice: a new system for collecting deliveries
readings.summary: Một tòa nhà thay đổi cách nhận và lấy hàng giao tận nơi. Thông báo giải thích giờ phục vụ, xác nhận người nhận, hàng quá khổ và cách phản hồi trong giai đoạn thử nghiệm.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Residents of Willow Court have recently received more deliveries than the reception shelves can hold. On several evenings, parcels covered part of the entrance, and residents had difficulty finding their own packages among similar boxes. The building team will therefore open a small collection room beside the laundry area next Monday. This notice explains how the room will operate during its first month. The aim is to make collection more organised without expecting reception staff to manage an unlimited amount of storage. Residents can still arrange direct delivery to their flats when they are at home and the delivery company offers that option.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The collection room will be staffed from seven to nine in the morning and from six to eight in the evening on weekdays. On Saturdays, it will open from ten until noon. There will be no regular collection period on Sundays. These times were chosen after a resident survey showed that many people leave early and return after normal office hours. The building team recognises that the schedule will not suit everyone. During the trial, residents who cannot attend any listed period can ask reception about an alternative appointment. Such appointments depend on staff availability and should be arranged before arriving to collect a parcel.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: When a parcel arrives, staff will record the flat number and attach a numbered label to the package. The resident will receive a message containing the same number and the next collection times. To collect it, residents should show the message and something displaying their name. Staff will compare the details before handing over the package. If a resident asks a neighbour to collect it, that resident should send reception the neighbour's name in advance. This extra step may take a little time, but it should reduce mistakes when people share a surname or when several deliveries arrive for one flat on the same day.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The room is intended for ordinary parcels that one person can move comfortably. Furniture, large appliances, and other oversized deliveries must go directly to the resident. Residents expecting such items should agree on a delivery time and be ready to meet the driver. Staff cannot leave large objects in the entrance while waiting for someone to return. Parcels requiring refrigeration will also be excluded because the room has no suitable equipment. Before ordering, residents should check whether their chosen delivery service needs a signature or has special handling requirements. The building team cannot promise that every kind of delivery will fit the new arrangement.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Ordinary parcels should be collected within three collection days of the arrival message. Sunday will not count as a collection day because the room is normally closed. If a resident is away, reception should be informed so that an agreed collection plan can be recorded. Staff will send one reminder before contacting the resident directly about a package that remains on the shelf. The team will not open parcels to identify their contents. Packages with an unreadable flat number will be kept separately while staff try to identify the recipient from the outside label. Residents should include their full flat number whenever they place an order.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: During the first week, there may be a queue because residents and staff will be learning the process. Please have the arrival message ready before reaching the desk. If a package appears damaged, staff will note its visible condition before collection, and the resident can decide what to do next with the seller or delivery company. The room's record confirms when staff received a package; it does not confirm what was inside it. Questions about missing contents should therefore be directed to the business responsible for the order. Reception can provide the recorded arrival time if that information helps the resident explain the problem.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: At the end of the month, the building team will review collection times, waiting periods, and the number of parcels left beyond the normal collection window. A comment sheet will be available beside the room, and residents may also send feedback through the building app. The review may lead to different opening hours or a limit on how many parcels can be stored for one flat. No decision has been made about these possible changes. Residents will receive an updated notice before any new arrangement begins. For now, clear address labels and prompt collection will help the small room serve the whole building more smoothly.

readings.title: Release plan: helping users recover unfinished forms
readings.summary: Một nhóm sản phẩm lên kế hoạch phát hành tính năng lưu bản nháp cho biểu mẫu dài. Bài đọc trình bày phạm vi lưu dữ liệu, cách thông báo trạng thái, thử nghiệm và tiêu chí tạm dừng phát hành.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The customer portal at Moss Services includes a request form with twelve sections. Users often need to leave it unfinished while they find an account number or ask a colleague for information. At present, leaving the page can mean starting again. Support received twenty-three messages about lost work last month, although these messages do not show how many users experienced the problem without reporting it. The product team has prepared a release plan for a draft-saving feature. Its aim is to help users continue an unfinished request while making the difference between a saved draft and a submitted request unmistakably clear.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The first version will save a draft only when the user selects the Save draft button. Automatic saving was considered, but the team decided that an explicit action would be easier to explain and test within the available time. After a successful save, a message will display the time and a link to the user's draft list. If saving fails, the form will stay open and show a message asking the user to try again. The interface must never display a successful save before the service confirms it. Otherwise, someone could leave the page believing their work was available when it was not.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Drafts will contain completed text fields and selected options, but uploaded attachments will not be included in this release. Supporting attachments would require additional work on storage and retrieval that the team cannot complete before the planned date. A notice beside the upload area will explain that files must be added again when a draft is reopened. Users will also see that notice before they save. This limitation is inconvenient, especially for requests involving several documents, but hiding it would create greater confusion. Support will receive an example showing how to explain the limitation and help a user check that all required files are present before submission.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: A saved draft will appear in the account's draft list for thirty days after its most recent save. The list will show the request title, the last saved time, and the date when the draft will be removed. Users can rename or delete a draft from that page. Submitting a request will remove its draft entry only after submission succeeds. This sequence matters because a failed submission should not destroy the user's remaining copy. The team will test saving and submission separately, including a case in which the user has two browser tabs open and returns to an older version of the form.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The release will begin with ten customer accounts whose administrators have agreed to participate. For five working days, support will record questions about finding drafts, missing attachments, and uncertainty over whether a request was submitted. Engineers will inspect failed-save reports using the account identifier and event time, without copying form answers into the report. The team wants enough information to investigate behaviour while keeping these reports focused on the process. The pilot participants will receive a short guide before the feature appears. They can continue using the existing form without saving a draft if that better suits their usual way of working.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The team has agreed on a clear pause condition. If a confirmed save cannot later be reopened, the pilot will pause while the cause is investigated. Minor wording problems can be corrected during the trial, but lost saved work would undermine the feature's main purpose. The existing submission process will remain available during a pause. Support will contact affected pilot accounts with the information engineers have confirmed and a practical next step. It should avoid promising recovery until the team has checked what remains available. The release owner, Priya, will decide when the pilot can resume after reviewing the investigation and the relevant checks.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: At the end of the pilot, Priya will prepare a recommendation for the product meeting. The decision will consider successful reopening, support questions, and how clearly users distinguish drafts from submissions. A large number of saved drafts alone will not prove that the feature works well. The team also needs to know whether people can return to useful work with confidence. If the pilot meets that standard, access will expand in stages over the following week. The attachment limitation will remain visible until a later release changes it. Any future automatic-saving proposal will be assessed separately using what the team learns from this simpler first version.

readings.title: Handover notes: keeping the supplier inbox moving
readings.summary: Mai chuẩn bị bàn giao hộp thư nhà cung cấp trong thời gian nghỉ. Ghi chú hướng dẫn phân loại thư, xử lý yêu cầu chưa rõ, giao trách nhiệm và quản lý công việc còn tồn đọng khi cô quay lại.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Mai will be away from the purchasing team for eight working days, starting next Thursday. During that period, Daniel will manage the shared supplier inbox each morning, and Ruth will cover it after lunch. The inbox receives delivery updates, questions about orders, and requests to change agreed dates. Although most messages are routine, an unclear reply can lead two people to make different arrangements with the same supplier. These notes describe the current process and the few open matters that need attention. They are intended to help the covering colleagues make consistent decisions without trying to reproduce every detail of Mai's normal working day.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Begin each shift by checking messages marked Waiting for us. These need a response from someone in the purchasing team. Messages marked Waiting for supplier have already received a question or request and usually need no immediate action. Read the latest exchange before replying, even if the subject line looks familiar. Suppliers sometimes reuse an old email conversation for a new order. Every reply should include the relevant order number in its first line. If no order number is available, ask for it before discussing quantities or dates. This makes it easier for both sides to confirm that they are talking about the same purchase.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The most time-sensitive open matter concerns the reusable display stands for the autumn exhibition. The supplier has offered delivery on Tuesday, but the events team needs the stands by Monday afternoon to complete its setup. Mai has asked whether part of the order can arrive earlier. Do not accept Tuesday delivery for the whole order without checking with the events coordinator, Elena. She may be able to use existing stands for some displays, but that decision belongs to her team. The latest supplier message and Elena's contact details are in the folder named Exhibition stands. Record any new agreement there as well as in the inbox.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: A second open matter is less urgent but could create unnecessary work. The stationery supplier sent an invoice for sixty boxes of paper, while the order record shows forty. The warehouse has confirmed that forty boxes arrived. Mai has asked the supplier to check the invoice and send a corrected version if appropriate. Until a reply arrives, leave the message marked Waiting for supplier and do not create a replacement order. The accounts team already knows about the difference. It needs the supplier's response before it can finish its own check, so forward that response to the shared accounts address when it arrives.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Routine delivery updates can be recorded without asking a manager, provided they do not change the agreed quantity, price, or deadline. A message saying that a driver will arrive in the morning rather than the afternoon normally falls into this category. However, a request for an extra payment or a later delivery date needs review by the purchasing lead. Do not describe a proposed change as accepted while that review is pending. A useful reply thanks the supplier, explains that the team is checking the proposal, and gives a realistic time for the next update. Avoid promising an answer before the responsible colleague is available.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Daniel and Ruth should use the inbox note field to hand work to each other. A good note states what happened, what remains unclear, and who will take the next step. Writing only Please check is unlikely to help a colleague who was not part of the earlier conversation. If a message needs specialist knowledge, assign it to the relevant person and tell the supplier when to expect an update. The covering colleague still owns the follow-up until that person accepts the task. This prevents messages from disappearing between teams simply because somebody forwarded them and assumed responsibility had moved with the email.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: On Mai's first morning back, the team will hold a fifteen-minute catch-up. Daniel and Ruth should prepare a short list of decisions made, outstanding questions, and any supplier who is still waiting for a promised reply. There is no need to describe every message that was handled successfully. Mai will read the notes for background and take back open tasks after the catch-up. If a covering colleague has already arranged a final call, that colleague should complete it and then update the record. Keeping the final step with the person who arranged it should give the supplier a smoother experience and avoid another unnecessary introduction.

readings.title: Repair estimate: deciding what a commuter bicycle needs
readings.summary: Một cửa hàng gửi báo giá sửa xe đạp cho người đi làm. Bài đọc phân biệt công việc đã kiểm tra và chưa xác nhận, các lựa chọn sửa chữa, chi phí và cách khách hàng quyết định trước khi cửa hàng thực hiện.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Thank you for bringing your bicycle to Riverbend Cycles on Wednesday. You explained that it is your main transport to work, a journey of about six kilometres each way, and that the gears sometimes hesitate when you change them. You also mentioned a clicking sound that is easier to hear when carrying your work bag. We completed an initial inspection this morning and have prepared two repair options below. This estimate separates work we can price now from checks that may reveal further problems. We have not started the repairs because you asked to review the likely cost and collection date first.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: During the inspection, the mechanic found a worn gear cable and a loose rear rack. Adjusting the cable improved the gear changes, but the cable's outer covering is damaged and should be replaced with the inner cable. The rack moved when pressure was applied, and tightening its fittings stopped one clicking sound during the workshop check. We cannot yet confirm that this was the only source of the noise because the bicycle has not been tested on the road with your usual bag. The estimate therefore includes a short test after the agreed work, rather than promising that every reported sound has already been explained.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Option One covers replacement of the gear cable and its outer covering, adjustment of the gears, checking the rack fittings, and the final road test. The total is 420,000 dong, including parts and labour. If you approve this option by noon on Friday, collection should be possible after four that afternoon because the required cable is already in stock. This option addresses the problems identified in the initial inspection. It does not include a full service of every part of the bicycle. We recommend it if your immediate priority is restoring normal gear changes while keeping this week's cost and time without the bicycle limited.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Option Two includes the same work plus a wider service covering wheel alignment, bearing checks, brake adjustment, and cleaning of the moving gear parts. The total is 760,000 dong, assuming those checks do not identify parts needing replacement. This option would require the bicycle to stay until Saturday afternoon. It may suit you if the bicycle has not had a general service for some time, but it should not be selected simply because it is more expensive. A wider check gives us more information; it does not mean that every checked part will need work. Your recent service record could help you choose between the options.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Neither price includes replacing tyres or the chain. We noted wear on the rear tyre, but this estimate does not include a decision about how soon to replace it. If you choose the wider service, the mechanic will examine it more closely and discuss the findings with you. Any additional parts or work will require your approval before we proceed. We will send a revised total and explain which part of the original estimate has changed. You can decline the additional work, although this may affect when the bicycle can be collected or what work can reasonably be completed during the visit.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Please reply with the option you prefer and a telephone number where we can reach you during the day. If a call is inconvenient, tell us when you can read messages so that a question does not leave the bicycle waiting unnecessarily. We can hold this estimate for seven days, but the collection times above depend on receiving approval by the stated deadline. Our courtesy bicycle is already reserved for Friday, so we cannot offer it for your journey home that day. If being without transport until Saturday would be difficult, the shorter repair option may better fit your immediate plans.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: At collection, the mechanic will explain the work completed and any checks that remain outstanding.
